title: Regional Evidence Aggregator & Retention Assertion Engine for SOC 2 / ISO Evidence Automation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a regional-aware evidence aggregation service and retention assertion engine that automatically maps SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls to concrete artifacts, enforces configured residency and retention policies, and produces auditor-ready ProofBundles. This work creates a centralized product-level orchestration layer that coordinates collectors, attaches immutable provenance metadata, applies retention TTLs per region, and exposes on-demand evidence packages for external auditors or internal compliance checks.
problem_statement: Right now evidence collection is ad hoc across services: retention TTLs are applied inconsistently, residency labels are scattered, and assembling a single auditor-ready artifact bundle requires manual runs and ad-hoc scripts. This causes long audit prep times, risk of mis-mapped controls, and potential compliance gaps for region-bound data.
goals: Provide a single service (Regional Evidence Aggregator) that orchestrates evidence collectors by region and control mapping
Implement a Retention Assertion Engine that evaluates configured retention policies and stamps artifacts with enforcement decisions
Produce immutable ProofBundles that are time-stamped, hash-signed, and contain control-to-artifact mapping for SOC 2 / ISO audits
Minimize manual steps for auditors: enable on-demand bundle exports and a UI for traceability
Ensure PII-safe redaction flows and KMS-backed signing for artifact integrity
non_goals: Rewriting existing collectors (we will adapt via adapters)
Replacing storage backends; system integrates with S3/GCS/On-prem object stores
Implementing an auditor-facing portal beyond export and metadata views (future work)
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce two components: (1) Regional Evidence Aggregator (REA) that schedules and coordinates collector adapters per region and control, normalizes artifacts, and tags them with ResidencyTagger metadata; (2) Retention Assertion Engine (RAE) that consumes artifacts, applies retention policy DSL, marks enforcement actions (retain, scrub, delete), and produces ProofBundles with signed manifests and artifact fingerprints.
architecture_considerations: Adapters pattern for existing collectors to minimize collector changes
Immutable manifests: manifest JSON + versioned signature stored alongside artifacts
Region-aware queues to ensure collectors run against region-bound endpoints
Lightweight policy DSL for retention rules with precedence rules (customer overrides, legal hold, archive)
Audit logging to Console with per-artifact trace and token-level cost estimation for collection runs
acceptance_criteria: REA can run a scheduled collection across 3 regions and produce normalized artifacts with ResidencyTagger metadata
RAE evaluates retention policies in the DSL and emits enforcement actions; simulated delete results in 'marked_for_deletion' tag in storage
System produces a ProofBundle that contains a signed manifest, mapping of controls to artifact IDs, timestamps, and KMS signature
Exported ProofBundle can be ingested by auditors and includes metadata sufficient to verify model (control mapping, collection run id, collector versions)
Security review completed and KMS signing integrated with existing key management patterns
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Accidentally exposing PII during bundle export. Mitigation: built-in redaction/obfuscation adapters and mandatory review flag for PII-containing controls.
Risk: Inconsistent residency labels across services. Mitigation: ResidencyTagger will canonicalize region tags and surface conflicts to Console for triage.
Risk: High collection costs for large customers. Mitigation: cost estimator, sampling mode, and TTL-aware incremental collections to reduce token/storage costs.
Risk: Legal hold/retention conflicts. Mitigation: Policy precedence and explicit manual override flows recorded in audit log.
stakeholders: Platform Eng Leads: Mariana Ruiz, Eric Zhao
engineering_requirements: Collector adapter spec and SDK for fast integration
Manifest signing using KMS/HSM and stored as immutable object metadata
Retention policy evaluation engine with fast incremental evaluation
Storage backends support S3/GCS and on-prem connectors
APIs for on-demand ProofBundle generation and status polling
design_requirements: Console UI for collection runs and per-artifact traceability
ProofBundle export UX with preset formats (zip, tar, signed-manifest.json)
Conflict resolution flows for residency mismatches
Privacy-first redaction indicators and manual approval for PII artifacts
metrics_of_success: Reduce auditor prep time for SOC 2 by 60% for pilot customers
Automated coverage: 80% of mapped controls produce evidence via REA within first run
False-positive retention enforcement <= 1% across pilot dataset
Adoption: 5 customers on Dedicated or Private using ProofBundles within 3 months of release
launch_plan: MVP (alpha): adapters for 4 main collectors, ProofBundle generator, Console view - target pilot customers
Beta: expand collectors, retention DSL edge cases, KMS signing and legal-hold integration
GA: SLA for collection windows, multi-region scale, integration docs and audit playbook
open_questions: Should ProofBundles include hashed copies of artifacts or only references+signed manifest?
How to handle cross-region controls that reference aggregated logs spanning multiple residency zones?
What retention policy precedence rules are mandatory vs configurable by customer?

Identify 2 pilot customers and schedule onboarding for alpha (2w)
